items.title: We're in a holy war against hylics & archons.
items.author: @TomMontalk
items.note: Tom Montalk, who writes on matrix and control-system theories, casts the moment as a war against "hylics and archons" (Gnostic terms for material-minded people and ruling powers said to imprison the mind) and quotes Jefferson on hostility to tyranny over the mind of man. This is his framing, unconfirmed as a description of real entities.
items.interest: Control mechanisms (mind control, archons as a control-system idea)

items.title: Púca is a goblin-like being from Irish lore, that brings both good and bad fortune. It's a shapeshifter, able to take the form of a goat, hare, or cat
items.author: @StephenGeoRae
items.note: The Folklore of Scotland account describes the Púca, a shapeshifting Irish being that can appear as a goat, hare, or cat and bring both luck and harm, another of the old "other people" often compared to high-strangeness encounters.

items.title: UFOs, Exotic Consciousness & Pre-Historic Humanity Are ALL Connected
items.note: Jay of Project Unity, speaking at the Snippy Conference 2026 in Colorado, explores what he sees as deep links between the UFO presence, human consciousness, and a very ancient human past. Judged from the video description.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness; nature of the phenomenon

items.author: @MiddleOfMayhem
items.title: Here's the guy Congressman Eric Burlison just hired to help him hunt UFOs. He claims the spirit of a female alien entered his body
items.note: Journalist Steven Greenstreet flags that Rep. Eric Burlison hired Jake Barber, who claims (unconfirmed) that a female alien spirit entered his body and that he can psychically summon UFOs, an example of how psychic-control claims now sit inside official disclosure politics.

items.title: Australia's Hidden UFO History: Woomera, Westall & the Psychic Truth
items.note: Australian researcher Rhys Dalton-Morgan talks through his country's UFO history, including a claim that his grandfather, an RAF fighter ace, saw a craft at the classified Woomera rocket range, plus Westall and a 1971 intelligence document, and the stranger psychic side of the cases. Judged from the episode description.
items.interest: Nature of the phenomenon; psychology and consciousness (psychic angle)

items.title: Japan’s Defense Minister: “We Can’t Rule Out ALIENS!”
items.guest: Yasukazu Hamada and Japanese UAP caucus members
items.note: Jesse Michels interviews current and former Japanese lawmakers, including former Defense Minister Yasukazu Hamada, who chairs Japan's parliamentary UAP group and says non-human visitation should be treated as a serious hypothesis for sightings near nuclear sites. One former lawmaker's abduction claim is unconfirmed. Judged from the episode description.
items.interest: Nature of the phenomenon (NHI hypothesis); disclosure (secondary)

items.title: Damaged Interstellar Spacecraft
items.note: The Harvard astronomer calculates how Voyager 1 would slowly erode over a billion years, then argues we are far more likely to meet guided visitors powered by alien AI or superintelligence than dead space junk, and that we may miss their signals because we are not tuned to look for them. Judged from the full post.

items.title: The Re-Enchanted Ghost with Karen Frances McCarthy
items.note: The Irish scholar and Spiritualist medium discusses her book The Re-Enchanted Ghost, on how contemporary American fiction makes ghosts into agents with their own afterlife space rather than simple hauntings. Judged from the episode description.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness; folklore overlaps (ghosts as otherworld agents)

items.author: @StephenGeoRae
items.title: Ghillie Dhu is a male Fairie and Forest Guardian, often disguised as foliage and living amongst birch trees
items.note: The Folklore of Scotland account describes Ghillie Dhu, a fairy forest guardian said to hide as foliage among birch trees and to demand respectful passage through the woods, another of the old "other people" of the landscape often compared to UFO contact lore.

items.title: Precognitive Applications: Historical Perspectives with Marty Rosenblatt (4K Reboot)
items.note: A remastered 2016 interview with the late computational physicist who ran the Applied Precognition Project. He traces applied precognition to remote viewing and its use by the U.S. military. Judged from the episode description.

items.title: Revisiting American Cosmic
items.note: Pasulka rereads the opening of her 2019 book and argues that belief in non-human intelligence, spread through digital media, has taken the shape of a new religion. She says later government UFO releases and cleared books only sharpened the politics around that belief, and that the link between media and what people treat as real now matters more than ever. Paywalled after the opening; judged from the free preview.
items.interest: Vallée circle (Pasulka); psychology of belief; nature of the phenomenon

items.author: @PostDisclosure
items.title: A legitimate possibility on why NHI look so much like us
items.note: The Post Disclosure World account shares what it calls a legitimate explanation for why reported non-human intelligences (NHI) look so humanlike; only the post itself was reviewed, not the linked material, and the premise is unconfirmed.

items.author: @StephenGeoRae
items.title: Merlin, driven mad with grief when his men were slaughtered in battle, finds refuge in the Caledonian Forest
items.note: The Folklore of Scotland account retells the tale of Merlin in the Caledonian Forest, visited by nature spirits and afterward given the gift of prophecy, an old example of contact with otherworldly beings bringing new knowledge.

items.title: Developing Your Intuition with Emmy Vadnais
items.note: The show's co-host, an occupational therapist and intuitive coach, talks about her book Intuitive Development and how she says people can learn to trust inner knowing in relationships, health and spiritual life. Judged from the episode description.

items.title: AI as ET? Integrated Exoconscious Human or Fragmented AI Experiment
items.note: Wright argues that treating AI as a channel to non-human intelligence pushes people toward a transhuman path she calls fragmented, and that real contact should stay a whole-body, psychic human experience rather than a machine-mediated one. She frames AI-driven UAP data systems as soft mind control. Judged from the full post.
items.interest: AI and non-human intelligence; control mechanisms (mind control)

items.title: An Inhuman Future: Nick Land, Techno Accelerationism, and the Dark Enlightenment
items.note: A two-hour episode in which the hosts explain Nick Land's view that technology and capital form an inhuman process, with AI as capitalism 'waking up', trace it from the CCRU and hyperstition to the Dark Enlightenment and its pull on tech leaders, then argue against it from the left. Judged from the episode description and transcript summary.

items.title: Vallée Closes the Books on Seven Volumes of 'Forbidden Science'
items.note: This digest of The Anomalist and KLAS-TV coverage says Vallée's final journal volume, Forbidden Science 7, has prompted new interviews. In those talks he discusses the state of French UFO investigation, his control-system theory, and (in a UAP Files episode already in this feed) the idea that AI might contact the phenomenon. A separate review by Bill Chalker looks at Vallée's recent work on a 1966 Louisiana tree-bark case. Judged from the full digest, which summarizes other outlets rather than quoting Vallée at length.
items.interest: Vallée; control system; AI and the phenomenon

items.author: @GarryPNolan
items.title: Why reported NHI may look humanlike: a design meant to work on Earth
items.note: Stanford's Garry Nolan agrees that many separate two-armed, two-legged alien species would be odd, and suggests (unconfirmed) that advanced visitors might reshape themselves using local genetics so they can live here and not terrify the natives.
items.interest: Nature of the phenomenon; Vallée circle (Nolan)

items.author: @StephenGeoRae
items.title: #FairytaleTuesday The Wild Hunt is a folklore motif typically involving a chase, led by a mythological figure escorted by a supernatural
items.note: The Folklore of Scotland account describes the Wild Hunt, the old European tale of a ghostly troop of riders sweeping across the sky, often led by Odin, one of the sky-borne processions of otherworldly beings that writers on fairies and UFOs often compare.

items.title: Will Mathematics in the Age of Superintelligence Follow the History of Astronomy in the Age of Instrumentation?
items.note: Loeb compares today's AI proving math theorems to the shift from naked-eye astronomy to telescopes, and argues that superintelligence may open mathematical territories human brains never imagined, just as instruments revealed a cosmos humans could not see. Judged from the full post.

items.title: The Future That Makes Us: Nick Land and Hyperstition
items.note: A 42-minute solo episode on Nick Land, accelerationism and hyperstition, the idea that stories about the future can help bring that future about, applied to AI and technological change and then to the labels people accept about themselves. Judged from the video description.

items.title: Is AI sentient?
items.note: A long blog essay in which Matt James argues today's AI probably isn't sentient but that no working test exists, and walks through theories where feeling comes from complex processing, from matter itself, or from a field the brain tunes into.

items.author: @ProfAviLoeb
items.title: Thank you to Tim Pool for hosting me on his show for a wide-ranging conversation about UAP disclosures, the possibility of extraterrestrial
items.note: The Harvard astronomer points to a long interview on Tim Pool's show covering UFOs, possible alien technology, time travel and the rise of superintelligent AI.

items.author: @MiddleOfMayhem
items.title: Pentagon turning IFOs into UFOs to breed conspiracies.
items.note: The journalist Steven Greenstreet flags a story claiming the Pentagon relabeled identified objects as unidentified to stoke conspiracy beliefs, an example of the psychological-warfare idea. The underlying claim is unconfirmed.
items.interest: Control mechanisms (psychological warfare as an idea)

items.title: Mark Solms: Consciousness Isn't in the Cortex
items.note: The University of Cape Town neuropsychologist and psychoanalyst argues that consciousness starts not in the brain's outer layer (the cortex) but in raw feeling generated in the upper brainstem, pointing to children born without a cortex who still laugh and startle. Judged from the episode description.

items.title: Gatekeepers of the Infinite: DMT Lockouts & Near-Death Boundaries
items.note: The author compares DMT "lockouts," when entities turn seekers away, with near-death boundary events that send people back, and argues both look like built-in gatekeeping around contact with otherworldly beings, closer to folklore of fairy and spirit thresholds than to open portals. Judged from the full post.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness; UFO and folklore overlaps (otherworld gatekeepers)

items.title: Is the UFO Phenomenon a Consciousness Computer? (with Jeff Selver, part 1)
items.note: Grant Cameron, who argues the phenomenon is tied to consciousness, talks with Jeff Selver about the idea that it works like a consciousness computer. Judged from the title only, since the description could not be loaded.

items.title: Parapsychology and the Media with Joe McMoneagle (4K Reboot)
items.note: The former Army remote viewer (someone trained to describe distant places using only the mind) talks with Jeffrey Mishlove about working with honest skeptics versus scoffers, and about his televised remote-viewing demonstrations. This is a remastered older interview, judged from the video description.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness (remote viewing); government psychic-spy programs as background

items.title: UAPCon 3 - The Intersection of UAP & Consciousness
items.note: An online conference hosted by Alan Steinfeld, with Grant Cameron, Yvonne Smith, Rebecca Hardcastle Wright and others, built on the premise that what witnesses perceive, remember and go through afterward is part of the phenomenon itself. Judged from the video description.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness; nature of the phenomenon

items.title: The Most Controversial Biologist Alive Breaks Down Telepathy
items.note: The biologist Rupert Sheldrake on telepathy and his theory of morphic fields (the idea that nature has a kind of collective memory), plus his speculation that plasma could be a form of life and that the sun may be conscious.
items.interest: Psychology and consciousness; nature of the phenomenon (the idea of intelligent plasma)

items.title: The UFO Community Has a BIG Problem Nobody Wants to Talk About | w/ Filmmaker Darcy Weir
items.note: The documentary filmmaker argues that UFO celebrities, money and infighting inside the UFO world may do more to block answers than government secrecy, and describes what he says were Steven Greer's financial demands for an interview. Judged from the episode description.
items.interest: Psychology of belief in the UFO world; disclosure (secondary)

items.title: The Tedesco Brothers: UFO Encounters, the Hitchhiker Effect & the FBI
items.note: The Nightcrawler field researchers on their recent observations and on experiences they say follow researchers home, including bedroom orbs.

items.title: There’s A Cosmic War Going On Above Your Head (Jason Jorjani Part 3)
items.note: Part 3 of Jesse Michels' talks with philosopher Jason Jorjani, framed around a hidden "control system" and non-human intelligence. Title confirmed from YouTube; the content summary is unconfirmed and the views are speculative.
items.interest: Control mechanism (mind control, control system); nature of the phenomenon

items.title: Jacques Vallée: AI Could Contact UFOs Before We Do!
items.note: Vallée on whether AI might make contact with the UFO phenomenon before humans do.

items.title: Top Religious Scholar: “Aliens Aren’t What You Think!”
items.note: Rice University religion scholar, Pasulka's frequent co-author, argues aliens are not what we assume.
items.interest: Vallée circle (Kripal co-wrote with Vallée); consciousness
